sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 26.0% a year from $4.32 billion in FY2016 to $34.6 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F231].
The path was a step change, not a straight line: revenue rose 68.3% in FY2021 and 43.6% in FY2022, fell 3.9% in FY2023, then grew 13.7% and 34.3% in FY2024 and FY2025 [D258][D314][D370][D426][D483].
The FY2022 jump included Xilinx embedded product revenue, which lifted Embedded net revenue to $4.6 billion from $246 million [P41].
The FY2023 decline came from a 25% fall in Client revenue on weak PC demand and inventory correction, plus a 9% fall in Gaming semi-custom sales [P35].
Data Center was the largest driver, contributing 15.7pp of FY2025's 34.3% revenue growth on 32.2% segment growth and 48.0% of revenue [D694][D483][D693][D692].
The filing attributes that growth to strong demand for 5th generation AMD EPYC processors and AMD Instinct MI350 Series GPUs [P15].
Client and Gaming contributed 19.0pp in FY2025, with Client at 30.7% of revenue and Gaming at 11.3% [D701][D754][D761].
Client revenue rose on a 31% increase in processor unit shipments and a 15% increase in average selling price, while Gaming gained on semi-custom revenue and Radeon GPUs [P10][P9].
Operating costs grew 10.0pp slower than revenue in FY2025, at 24.3%, and incremental operating margin was 20.3% [D512][D504][D511].
Operating margin of 10.7% in FY2025 sits above the 7.2% window median but far below the 22.2% FY2021 high [F60][D795][D794].
Gross margin of 49.5% is a window high, above the 44.7% median [F40][D800][D801].
The FY2025 gross margin gain of 0.2pp came from product mix, partly offset by about $440 million of MI308 inventory and export-control charges [D498][P14].
In FY2025 net margin of 12.5% sat 1.9pp above the 10.7% operating margin, helped by $577 million of other income and a $103 million tax benefit [F80][F60][D843][X123][X113].
Operating cash flow of $7.71 billion was 1.78x net income in FY2025, above the 1.61x window median, and free cash flow was 1.55x net income [F110][F70][D470][D833][D471].
Operating cash flow included a $2.2 billion inventory increase to support the Data Center ramp [P3].
Free cash flow margin of 19.4% is near the 19.6% window high, with capex at 2.8% of revenue and 1.87x D&A [D467][D803][D466][D472].
Stock-based compensation of $1.64 billion was 21.2% of operating cash flow [X83][D473].
Net cash was $6.46 billion, or 18.6% of revenue, against a -17.3% peer median and the 100th percentile of five semis peers [D476][D477][D845][D844].
Total debt rose 138% to $4.10 billion after $1.5 billion of notes were issued in March 2025 [D475][D508][P6].
Buybacks of $1.32 billion were 19.5% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count was flat at -0.1% [X150][D479][D506].
The current ratio of 2.85x is a window high, above the 2.19x median [F210][D812][D813].
Revenue fell 3.9% in FY2023, the only decline in the window [R1][D370].
The drop was a PC inventory cycle rather than a structural loss of share, since revenue recovered 13.7% and 34.3% in the next two years [D426][D483].
Total debt rose 138% in FY2025 to $4.10 billion from $1.72 billion [R2][D475][D418].
The increase is covered by $10.6 billion of cash and investments, so leverage remains modest [D474].
Days inventory outstanding rose to 165 days in FY2025 from 160 days in FY2024 [D481][D424].
Inventory build is the working-capital item to watch, since it absorbed $2.2 billion of cash in FY2025 [P3].
Whether operating margin holds above the 7.2% window median in the FY2026 10-K [D795].
Whether days inventory outstanding falls below the 165 days reported for FY2025 in the next 10-K [D481].
Whether net cash as a share of revenue stays above the 18.6% FY2025 level as debt matures [D477].
